datasets_from_scratch_no_english_source.evidence: All content was created in English first: 'We opted to create multiple-choice questions and answers in English and then translate' (Section 3). Passages sourced from FLORES-200, originally English from Wikinews, Wikijunior, WikiVoyage.

datasets_translated_from_english.evidence: We opted to create multiple-choice questions and answers in English and then translate, as opposed to creating resources natively in each language. (Section 3)

details.Belebele: Explicitly not culturally grounded. 'by-design the samples collected do not capture language- and culture-specific phenomena such as formality, values, and aboutness. While conscious of this Western-centrism, BELEBELE was designed to prioritize comparability across languages.' (Ethics Statement)

all_annotators_native_speakers.evidence: BELEBELE was created end-to-end without the use of machine translation technology, relying solely on experts fluent in English and the target language. (Section 3.3); The [FLORES-200] translations were performed by native speakers with high English fluency and translation experience. (Section 2.4); All translations were proofread and edited by an additional annotator. (Section 3.3)

annotator_workforce.evidence: We implement an iterative procedure with the Language Service Provider (LSP) for this involved data collection task (Section 3.1). English MCQs created by annotators through LSP with 5 iterations of feedback. Translations done by experts fluent in English and target language, proofread by additional annotator. No details on annotator demographics, compensation, or IRB review provided.

cultural_flags.english_centricity_notes: The benchmark is explicitly English-centric by design. All questions and answers created in English, then translated. Passages from FLORES-200 originate from English Wikipedia sources. The Ethics Statement acknowledges: 'by-design the samples collected do not capture language- and culture-specific phenomena such as formality, values, and aboutness. While conscious of this Western-centrism, BELEBELE was designed to prioritize comparability across languages.' Evaluation prompts and instructions also in English for LLM experiments.

notably_excluded: Indigenous languages of the Americas (only Guarani included)
geographic_representation.evidence: The dataset covers typologically diverse languages across 29 scripts and 27 language families. (Section 1); 122 language variants from around the world. Appendix A.1 lists all languages showing broad global coverage but concentration in Indo-European (50 languages), Atlantic-Congo (16), and Afro-Asiatic (16).
